title: Boston World Cup committee says tailgating will be allowed at Gillette Stadium despite previous ban
content:
The Boston 2026 World Cup host committee has announced that tailgating will be permitted at Gillette Stadium despite it previously stating it would be banned.

The organizing committee had said on its website that the popular pre-game ritual would not be allowed due to “FIFA policy”. This was met with significant criticism online, with tailgating routinely held before the New England Patriot’s home NFL games at the same stadium.

On Monday, however, a Boston spokesperson said that the committee had “sought clarification” from FIFA, world football’s governing body, and announced the pre-game social event would be allowed at the stadium as there are no “venue restrictions or local public safety restrictions” to prevent it from happening.

The spokesperson explained it had initially included the tailgating ban on its website as the committee’s understanding had been that prohibiting tailgating was a tournament-wide rule enforced by FIFA.

“Based on prior information that FIFA communicated to Boston Soccer 2026, it was both our understanding and the host venue’s understanding that ‘no tailgating’ was a tournament-wide FIFA rule, and we included that information in our forward-facing messaging accordingly,” the spokesperson said.

“In light of FIFA’s recent comments, we sought clarification from FIFA in order to provide the best fan experience possible,” the statement continued. “We are pleased to share that tailgating will be permitted at Boston Stadium like any other event hosted at the stadium as there are no venue restrictions or local public safety restrictions in place that would prohibit it. Additional fan information will be shared ahead of the start of the tournament.”

Tailgating is a pre-game social event hosted in stadium parking lots before games, across a range of North American sports, with fans typically congregating many hours before the match begins to consume food and drink.

The language on Boston’s organising committee’s website initially attributed the banning of tailgating to “FIFA policy”, but the website was subsequently updated and the reference to a “FIFA policy” removed.

FIFA sources, speaking on the condition of anonymity to protect relationships, had said the governing body will work with local authorities to determine what is and isn’t safe before a decision is made on whether tailgating is allowed at each venue.

Tailgating will not be permitted at Lumen Field in Seattle due to its city centre location, but the pre-match gatherings are also banned during the NFL season.
